title: Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2020
official_summary:
Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2020

This bill modifies administrative provisions related to the bankruptcy trustee system. Specifically, the bill (1) provides for the distribution of bankruptcy fees made to the U.S. Trustee System Fund for the costs of administering payments and trustee compensation, (2) establishes the Chapter 7 Trustee Fund and associated fees, and (3) extends the temporary office of bankruptcy judges in specified judicial districts.

summary.headline: A 2021 law that adjusts how the federal bankruptcy trustee system is funded, how trustees are paid, and how some bankruptcy judgeships are staffed.
summary.what_it_does: The law sets rules for how bankruptcy fees are distributed into the U.S. Trustee System Fund, which pays for the costs of administering trustee payments and trustee compensation. It creates a Chapter 7 Trustee Fund and related fees. It also extends the temporary positions of bankruptcy judges in certain judicial districts.

who_it_affects.group: People filing for bankruptcy under Chapter 7
who_it_affects.how: They pay bankruptcy fees that help fund the trustee system and the new Chapter 7 Trustee Fund.
The law changes how their compensation is paid and funded through the trustee system.

who_it_affects.group: Bankruptcy judges in specified judicial districts
who_it_affects.how: Their temporary positions are extended under the law.
The law sets how fees are distributed to pay for administering trustee payments and compensation.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 12, 2021. The official summary does not list other specific effective dates.
